Alex Kim: Hey @people-ops — planning to relocate to Mexico (CDMX) mid-May. Quick questions: what happens to the monthly WFH stipend, equipment reimbursement window, and taxes? Do I need to switch to local payroll or can I stay on US payroll for a bit? Also worried about whether this creates any tax/nexus issues for Redwood if more folks move there. Any docs I should start now? Thanks!

Jenna (People Ops): Congrats Alex! Short version: stipend is pro-rated for partial months, equipment must be claimed within 30 days of move, and payroll depends on timing + employment law. We should collect your move date and new address. I'll outline steps below and we can DM for details.

Jenna (People Ops): ```Quick checklist:
- Submit "Location Change" in HiBob with effective move date
- Attach new local address + preferred bank details
- People Ops will open an International Payroll intake + benefits review
- Equipment reimbursement: submit receipts in Expensify within 30 days of shipment/receipt
- WFH stipend: pro-rated for the month of move and paid on next payroll run
- If you remain on US payroll while living in MX >90 days, we need to evaluate tax/social security and Nexus implications
- If >2-3 employees in MX, we will engage Legal for country entity/PE review
```

Alex Kim: Thanks — what's the standard stipend amount for Mexico? And is the stipend taxable there (MX) vs US if I stay on US payroll? Also curious if healthcare benefits transfer.

Sam Patel: Usually the standard WFH stipend is $100/month (USD) unless you negotiated something different. Key points: the stipend itself is treated as taxable income in whichever country you are tax resident in. If you stay on US payroll temporarily, it will be reported on US taxes/payroll; if we transition you to Mexico payroll, local tax rules apply and payroll withholdings will change. We can run a short simulation once we have dates.

Priya Rao (Legal): Adding a legal note: one-off moves are usually fine, but we track headcount by country. If several employees relocate to Mexico, that could create local corporate or permanent establishment considerations. We will flag if the headcount or activities cross thresholds and coordinate with Tax/Finance. For the move itself we need: government ID, proof of address, and local bank details to set up local payroll if you choose that route.

payroll-bot: Please complete the International Payroll Intake form so Payroll can advise on timeline and withholding: https://redwood.example/international-payroll-intake (this auto-creates the payroll ticket once submitted).

Jenna (People Ops): On benefits: if you stay on US benefits while physically in MX, some plans will not cover care locally. We can provide localized benefit options or a benefits-stipend top-up in some cases. We'll do a benefits eligibility check once you submit the location change.

Alex Kim: Got it — I'll submit the HiBob change today and fill the payroll intake form. One last thing: is there a proration rule for relocation stipend vs WFH stipend if the company helps with relocation?

Jenna (People Ops): Relocation assistance (if approved) is handled separately and usually paid as a one-time lump sum or reimbursed with receipts. WFH stipend proration is independent (monthly pro-rate). If you get relocation pay, we will note tax treatment in the relocation package doc. We'll follow up with a 15-min call to walk the specifics once your forms are in.

Alex Kim: Perfect — thanks everyone, I'll DM the move date and drop the forms in now. :thumbsup:
